guidance.heading: FISCAL 2027 OUTLOOK SUMMARY
section: •Compass Minerals expects continued earnings improvement in fiscal 2027, driven mainly by stronger Salt pricing, an improved customer mix, and further reductions in per-ton production costs. Total adjusted EBITDA guidance is $250 million to $290 million on revenue of $1.2 billion to $1.28 billion. The $270 million midpoint represents approximately 15% growth over fiscal 2026.
•Guidance range for Salt segment adjusted EBITDA in 2027 is $255 million to $281 million.

◦The fiscal 2027 Salt outlook reflects a deliberate focus on value over volume. Stronger highway pricing, improved customer mix and lower per-ton production costs at the North American assets are expected to more than offset lower planned sales volumes and higher fuel-driven logistics costs. At the midpoint, Salt adjusted EBITDA per ton is expected to increase more than 29% and Salt adjusted EBITDA margin to expand approximately 400 basis points.
•Guidance range for Plant Nutrition segment adjusted EBITDA in 2027 is $49 million to $59 million.

◦The segment is expected to generate adjusted EBITDA at the midpoint in line with 2026 on sales volumes of 270,000 to 290,000 tons, with modestly higher pricing that maintains the premium of sulfate of potash (SOP) to muriate of potash.

◦The Ogden dryer and compaction project is expected to be completed in fiscal 2027. The project is designed to add capacity, improve product quality, reduce unit costs, and enhance long-term operating efficiency, with the majority of the financial benefit expected beginning in fiscal 2028.
•Guidance range for adjusted EBITDA related to corporate overhead and other is $(54) million to $(50) million.
•Interest expense is expected to be $60 million to $64 million.
•Capital expenditures are expected to be $105 million to $125 million, as the company invests first in the operational cost improvement it is driving and the long-term sustainability of its assets.

desk.headline: Revenue up 10% to $250.9m, beat; adjusted loss of $0.18/share, miss; fiscal 2027 outlook sees adjusted EBITDA of $250–290m
results: Q4 revenue rose to $250.9m from $227.5m; Salt revenue grew 13% to $204.6m on 7% higher volumes and 5% better pricing.
The quarter's net loss widened slightly to $8.1m ($0.19 per share) as higher tax offset a smaller pre-tax loss; adjusted loss was $0.18 per share.
For the full year the company returned to profit: net income of $17.5m against a $79.8m loss, and adjusted EBITDA up 18% to $235.1m.
Plant Nutrition adjusted EBITDA jumped 57% to $54.8m for the year, with margin up to 26.4% from 16.9%.
Total debt fell $65.0m to $767.2m and net leverage dropped to 3.2x from 3.9x; liquidity at year end was $247.2m.

guidance.summary: First outlook for fiscal 2027: adjusted EBITDA of $250–290m (about 15% growth at the midpoint) on revenue of $1.20–1.28bn, driven by higher salt prices and lower unit costs despite fewer tons sold.

points: CEO Edward Dowling credited better reliability, efficiency, pricing discipline and cost control for the improvement.
North American highway salt bids came in about 12% higher on price, with guaranteed terms rising to 78% of the US book from 65%.
Management is choosing value over volume: highway volumes are planned about 13% lower at the midpoint because salt supply is limited.
Priorities for 2027 are lower unit costs, turning price gains into margin, finishing key projects such as Ogden, and further debt reduction.
